[Download PDF](https://www.greenfireres.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Press-Release-Strathcona-Resources-Announces-Agreement-to-Acquire-Greenfire-Resources.pdf)


**Calgary, Alberta (November 8, 2026)** – Strathcona Resources Ltd. (“ **Strathcona** “) (TSX: SCR) and Greenfire Resources Ltd. (“ **Greenfire** “) (TSX: GFR, NYSE: GFR) today announced a definitive agreement (the “ **Arrangement Agreement** “) for Strathcona to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Greenfire (the “ **Transaction** “).


**Transaction Structure**


Under the terms of the Arrangement Agreement, Greenfire shareholders may elect to receive, at their election, either:


1. 25 shares of Strathcona for each share of Greenfire (the “ **GFR** **Share Option** “), equating to $9.09 per Greenfire share or a 15% premium to Greenfire’s closing share price on November 6, 2026 based on Strathcona’s closing price on the same day, or;


1. $11.00 in cash per Greenfire share (the “ **GFR** **Cash Option** “), equating to a 39% premium to Greenfire’s closing share price on November 6, 2026, or a 26% premium to Greenfire’s trailing 30-day volume-weighted-average price.


Neither the GFR Share Option nor the GFR Cash Option will be subject to proration, allowing all Greenfire shareholders to receive their election in full. Waterous Energy Fund (together with its affiliated funds, “ **WEF** “), the current holder of 72% of Greenfire’s outstanding shares and 57% of Strathcona’s outstanding shares, has signed a support agreement in favour of the Transaction under which it will elect to receive the GFR Share Option for its Greenfire shares.


Depending on the elections made by non-WEF Greenfire shareholders, Strathcona expects to issue between approximately 43 million and 60 million Strathcona shares to Greenfire shareholders (equating to 17% to 22% of the pro forma business) and pay cash consideration of up to approximately $740 million. Inclusive of Greenfire’s approximately $550 million of net debt(1) outstanding as of September 30, 2026, this equates to a total transaction value of approximately $2.7 to $2.9 billion(2), based on Strathcona’s closing share price as of November 6, 2026.


Strathcona expects the existing Greenfire leadership team to continue to lead day-to-day operations of Greenfire’s assets within a new Strathcona business unit – SCR Central Athabasca – with Colin Germaniuk, President of Greenfire, serving as President of SCR Central Athabasca. Like Strathcona’s three existing business units (SCR Cold Lake, SCR Lloydminster Thermal and SCR Lloydminster Conventional) SCR Central Athabasca will function semi-autonomously within Strathcona, to maximize accountability and operational performance.

**Strategic Rationale**


Benefits for Both Strathcona and Greenfire


1. *Unification of Two Complementary Businesses with Parallel Growth Plans* – The Transaction will bring together two long-life oil sands and heavy oil companies, better positioned to execute each company’s growth plans. Over the next five years Strathcona and Greenfire each plan to grow production at an 11-12% CAGR through a combination of drilling to fill existing facilities and brownfield expansions. Beyond 2031, both companies also have attractive brownfield and greenfield growth opportunities across prospective areas such as Plover Lake, Taiga, Glenbogie, Selina, Muriel Lake, Corner, and Chard. The improved access to capital of the combined business is expected to allow the acceleration of each of these standalone plans.


1. *Expanded SAGD Scale and Expertise* – The combined business will have over 3.0 billion barrels of proved plus probable (“ **2P** “) oil reserves, equating to a 2P reserves life index of 54 years, the longest of any publicly traded company in Canada (by approximately 20 years) upon closing. The combined business will be the 4th largest SAGD operator in Canada and the only company with significant operations across all three major oil sands deposits (Athabasca, Cold Lake and Lloydminster) and all major producing formations (the McMurray, Clearwater and Mannville). Strathcona expects the combined business to benefit from shared learnings and best practices across business units, driving improved operational performance.


1. *Unique Market Position* – The combined business will be the only publicly traded oil sands company with current oil sands production between 25 and 450 Mbbls / d, offering a more rapid growth profile than larger oil sands operators and a better capitalized, lower risk asset base than smaller oil sands operators. Strathcona will be the only oil sands operator without natural gas or downstream operations, providing investors the only long-life oil “pure play”.


Benefits for Strathcona


1. *Meaningful Synergies and Extended Tax Horizon:* Strathcona expects to realize approximately $75 million of annual run-rate synergies within the first year of combined operations, due to a combination of lower borrowing costs, procurement efficiencies, and the removal of duplicative public company costs. In addition, Greenfire’s $2.8 billion of tax pools ($2.0 billion of which are immediately deductible) are expected to allow Strathcona to extend its cash tax horizon from 2027 to 2031 at US$75 / bbl WTI, resulting in approximately $400 million of expected cash tax savings over the next four years.


1. *Accelerates Path to Investment Grade Credit Rating:* Strathcona expects the combined business will have the necessary size and scale to earn an investment grade credit rating in the Canadian bond market within one year of closing, lowering Strathcona’s cost of borrowing, reducing midstream costs, and increasing its financial flexibility.


1. *Immediately Accretive to Net Asset Value and Free Cash Flow:* The Transaction is expected to be approximately 6% accretive to Strathcona’s YE 2025 proved plus probable net asset value, after-tax per share (“ **2P NAV** “), including synergies, and immediately accretive to free cash flow after sustaining capital.


Benefits for Greenfire


1. *Option for Continued Participation in Strathcona on Accretive Basis:* The GFR Share Option share exchange ratio is directly in-line with the relative standalone 2P NAV of Strathcona and Greenfire. Inclusive of synergies, the GFR Share Option is expected to be immediately accretive to free cash flow after sustaining capital and approximately 3% accretive relative to Greenfire’s standalone 2P NAV.


1. *Participation in Lower Risk, Scaled Business:* The GFR Share Option provides Greenfire shareholders with the opportunity to participate in a larger, diversified business instead of a single-asset company, reducing single-event risk while increasing access to capital to accelerate organic growth.


1. *Option for Immediate Attractive Cash Premium:* The GFR Cash Option provides an attractive premium for Greenfire shareholders who are not looking for continued participation, reflective of the unique value and synergy opportunities Greenfire is contributing to Strathcona.


**Process and Approvals**


In considering the Transaction, the boards of directors of Strathcona and Greenfire each established a special committee composed of directors independent from WEF and management (the “ **Strathcona Special Committee** ” and the “ **Greenfire Special Committee** “, respectively) to consider, evaluate and oversee negotiations with respect to the Transaction and make a recommendation to its respective board with respect thereto. The Strathcona Special Committee engaged Jefferies Securities, Inc. (“ **Jefferies** “) as its financial advisor and Torys LLP as its legal advisor. The Greenfire Special Committee engaged CIBC Capital Markets (“ **CIBC** “) as its financial advisor and Norton Rose Fulbright Canada LLP as its legal advisor.


In connection with the Transaction, the Strathcona Special Committee supervised the preparation of and considered a formal valuation of Greenfire shares by Jefferies in accordance with Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“ **MI 61-101** ”) and received Jefferies’ opinion as to the fairness, from a financial point of view, to Strathcona of the consideration to be paid by Strathcona pursuant to the Transaction, in each case as of November 8, 2026, and based on and subject to various assumptions, qualifications, limitations and other matters (the “ **Jefferies Valuation and Opinion** ”). In connection with the Transaction, the Greenfire Special Committee supervised the preparation of and considered CIBC’s formal valuation of Greenfire’s and Strathcona’s shares prepared in accordance with MI 61-101 and received CIBC’s opinion that the consideration to be received by the non-WEF Greenfire Shareholders pursuant to the Arrangement Agreement was fair, from a financial point of view, to non-WEF Greenfire shareholders, in each case as of November 8, 2026, and based on and subject to various assumptions, qualifications, limitations and other matters (the “ **CIBC Valuation and Opinion** ”). Neither the formal valuations nor opinions of Jefferies or CIBC constitute a recommendation as to how to vote or act in connection with the Transaction or any other matter.


The Strathcona Special Committee evaluated the Transaction with the assistance of management and legal and financial advisors and has unanimously determined, and the Strathcona board of directors (with interested directors abstaining), based on the unanimous recommendation of the Strathcona Special Committee, has determined, that the Transaction is in the best interests of Strathcona and is fair to non-WEF Strathcona shareholders. The Greenfire Special Committee evaluated the Transaction with the assistance of management and legal and financial advisors and has unanimously determined, and the Greenfire board of directors (with interested directors abstaining), based on the unanimous recommendation of the Greenfire Special Committee, has determined, that the Transaction is in the best interests of Greenfire and is fair to non-WEF Greenfire shareholders.


The Arrangement Agreement includes customary deal protection provisions, including that each party has agreed not to solicit or initiate any discussions regarding any other transaction, subject to customary “fiduciary out” rights to respond to a superior proposal. Strathcona and Greenfire have also granted each other a right to match any superior proposal and each has agreed to pay a termination fee to the other party if the Arrangement Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances.


The Transaction is to be effected by way of a plan of arrangement under the *Business Corporations Act* (Alberta) (the “ **Arrangement** ”). A joint information circular for the special meetings of shareholders of Strathcona and Greenfire to consider the Transaction is expected to be mailed in late November 2026 and will be available on both company websites, as well as on SEDAR+. Strathcona, Greenfire and WEF will also jointly prepare and file with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “ **SEC** “) a transaction statement on Schedule 13E-3 (the “ **Schedule 13E-3** ”). A copy of the Arrangement Agreement will also be available on SEDAR+ and, in the case of Greenfire, on EDGAR. All shareholders are urged to read the joint information circular once available as it will contain additional important information concerning the Transaction and the special meetings of shareholders of Strathcona and Greenfire, including the deadline for making elections to receive the GFR Cash Option or the GFR Share Option.


The Transaction is subject to approval of not less than two-thirds of the votes cast at each of the Strathcona and Greenfire shareholder meetings, and the fulfilment of other conditions that are typical for transactions of this nature, including *Competition Act* approval. In addition, the Transaction is subject to minority shareholder approval under MI 61-101 for both Strathcona and Greenfire, being a simple majority of votes cast at their respective shareholder meetings, excluding votes cast by WEF and other shareholders required to be excluded pursuant to MI 61-101 and, in the case of Strathcona, the TSX. In addition to shareholder approvals, the Transaction is subject to regulatory approvals, including the approval of the TSX and the approval of the Court of King’s Bench of Alberta. The special meetings of the shareholders of each of Strathcona and Greenfire are expected to be held in January 2027, with closing expected shortly thereafter, provided that the required court, shareholder and regulatory approvals described above have been obtained.


Greenfire shareholders who elect the GFR Share Option will receive a dividend on closing equal to the regular quarterly dividends paid by Strathcona between today and closing, payable on a per share basis on their pro forma Strathcona shares. The dividend will be declared by Strathcona following Strathcona’s acquisition of Greenfire and as part of the Transaction. Following Strathcona’s acquisition of Greenfire, as part of the Transaction, Greenfire will be amalgamated into Strathcona, with the combined entity continuing as Strathcona Resources Ltd.


WEF has signed a support agreement in favour of the Transaction, committing to vote all of its Strathcona and Greenfire shares in favour of the Transaction at the relevant shareholder meetings, and to elect for the GFR Share Option for its Greenfire shares. Upon completion of the Transaction, WEF will hold between 60% and 64% of the shares of Strathcona, depending on the elections made by non-WEF Greenfire shareholders.


In addition, all non-WEF board members and executive officers of Strathcona and Greenfire, including independent directors, have signed support agreements in favour of the Transaction.


Following completion of the Transaction, it is expected that the Greenfire common shares will be delisted from the TSX and the New York Stock Exchange (the “ **NYSE** ”), and that Greenfire will cease to be a reporting issuer under Canadian securities laws in all provinces of Canada and that the Greenfire shares will be deregistered with the SEC. Strathcona does not intend to list its shares on the NYSE following the Transaction.


**Early Warning Reporting**


WEF has not acquired or disposed of any securities of Strathcona or Greenfire. As a result of its entry into the support agreement in favour of the Transaction, WEF will file amended early warning reports in accordance with *National Instrument 62-104 – Take-Over Bids and Issuer Bids* and *National Instrument 62-103 – The Early Warning System* and Related Take-Over Bid and Insider Reporting Issues to reflect a change in a material fact contained in its most recently filed reports. The reports will be filed electronically with the applicable securities regulatory authority in each province of Canada and will be available on SEDAR+ at[www.sedarplus.ca](http://www.sedarplus.ca/) . WEF will also file an amendment to its Schedule 13D with the SEC in respect of its holdings of Greenfire shares, which will be available on EDGAR at[www.sec.gov](http://www.sec.gov/) . For further information or to obtain a copy of the early warning reports, please contact WEF’s Chief Executive Officer at 403-930-6048 orinfo@waterous.com . The head office of WEF is located at 600, 301 – 8th Avenue SW, Calgary, Alberta T2P 1C5.


**Important Additional Information and Where to Find It**


In connection with the Transaction, Strathcona and Greenfire intend to file relevant materials on SEDAR+ and, for Greenfire, with the SEC on EDGAR, including the Schedule 13E-3. Shareholders will be able to obtain these documents, as well as other filings containing information about Strathcona, Greenfire, the Transaction and related matters, without charge, from the SEDAR+ website at www.sedarplus.ca and from the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov.


**Advisors**


Jefferies served as financial advisor and Torys LLP as legal advisor to the Strathcona Special Committee. CIBC Capital Markets served as financial advisor and Norton Rose Fulbright Canada LLP as legal advisor to the Greenfire Special Committee. J.P. Morgan served as financial advisor and Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP as legal advisors to Strathcona. RBC Capital Markets served as financial advisor and Bennett Jones LLP and Scale LLP as legal advisors to Greenfire.

****** ***Oil and Gas Advisory***


Unless indicated otherwise, production volumes and per-unit statistics are presented throughout this press release on a “gross” basis as determined in accordance with National Instrument 51-101 – *Standards for Disclosure for Oil and Gas Activities* (“ **NI 51-101** “), which is each company’s gross working interest basis before deduction of royalties and without including any royalty interests of such company. This press release makes assumptions relating to future production volumes based on reserve evaluation calculations prepared by third-party independent evaluators. Statements relating to reserves are deemed to be forward-looking statements as they involve the implied assessment, based on certain estimates and assumptions, that the reserves described can be profitably produced in the future. There are numerous uncertainties inherent in estimating quantities of 2P reserves and in projecting future rates of production. The total amount or timing of actual future production may vary significantly from reserves and production estimates. Uncertainties and risk factors are described in Strathcona’s Annual Information Form dated March 11, 2026 (the “ **Strathcona AIF** “) and Greenfire’s Annual Information Form dated March 12, 2026 (the “ **Greenfire AIF** “), and from time to time in each company’s public disclosure documents, which are available on the respective company’s SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca and, in the case of Greenfire, in its annual report on Form 40-F filed with the SEC, which is available on Greenfire’s EDGAR profile at[www.sec.gov](http://www.sec.gov/) .


Reserves estimates of Strathcona are based on the evaluations of McDaniel & Associates Consultants Ltd. (“ **McDaniel** “), independent reserves evaluator for Strathcona, as of December 31, 2025 and in accordance with the Canadian Oil and Gas Evaluation Handbook (the “ **COGE Handbook** “), and contained in the independent engineering evaluation of Strathcona’s petroleum and natural gas reserves prepared by McDaniel effective December 31, 2025 (the “ **Strathcona Report** “) and presented in accordance with NI 51-101 in the Strathcona AIF. Reserves estimates of Greenfire are based on: (a) the evaluations of McDaniel, independent reserves evaluator for Greenfire, as of December 31, 2025 and in accordance with the COGE Handbook, and contained in the independent engineering evaluation of Greenfire’s bitumen reserves in its Hangingstone facilities prepared by McDaniel effective December 31, 2025 (the “ **Greenfire Report** “) and presented in accordance with NI 51-101 in the Greenfire AIF; and (b) the evaluations of GLJ Ltd. (“ **GLJ** “), independent reserves evaluator for Connacher Oil and Gas Limited (“ **Connacher** “), as of December 31, 2025 and in accordance with the COGE Handbook, and contained in the independent engineering evaluation of all of Connacher’s oil, natural gas liquids and natural gas interests prepared by GLJ dated March 31, 2026, with an effective date of December 31, 2025 (the “ **Connacher Report** “). References to reserves of Greenfire represent the arithmetic sum of the reserves estimates of Greenfire and Connacher on a standalone basis, and references to pro forma or combined production and reserves of Strathcona and Greenfire represent the arithmetic sum of each company’s respective production volumes and reserves estimates on a standalone basis, and in each case do not account for any potential synergies or adjustments that may result from Greenfire’s acquisition of Connacher or the Transaction, as applicable, except for pro forma taxes based on the combined company’s tax pools. In addition, adjustments arising from differences among the Strathcona Report, the Greenfire Report and the Connacher Report, such as differences in the professional judgments underlying the reserves estimates, level of development, capital requirements, operating costs and other relevant considerations, may adversely affect the pro forma addition of reserves.


Reserves information in respect of Connacher has been obtained from Connacher and has not been independently verified. While Greenfire does not have any knowledge that such information may not be accurate, there can be no assurance that such information is complete or accurate. Greenfire makes no representation or warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of such information.


This press release contains certain oil and gas metrics, such as “reserves life index”, “PV-10” and “TEV / bbls / d”, which do not have standardized meanings or standard methods of calculation and therefore such measures may not be comparable to similar measures used by other companies and should not be used to make comparisons. Such metrics have been included herein to provide readers with additional measures to evaluate the Transaction; however, such measures are not reliable indicators of future performance and future performance may not compare to performance in previous periods and therefore such metrics should not be unduly relied upon. Reserves life index is calculated by dividing total gross 2P reserves by annualized YTD 2026 production. “PV-10” reflects the applicable independent reserves evaluator’s estimated after-tax net present value of future net revenue attributable to 2P reserves, discounted at 10%, as at December 31, 2025, excluding synergies. “TEV / bbls / d” is calculated by dividing total enterprise value by production for a given time period.


References to “oil” in this press release include bitumen and heavy oil. References to “Mbbls / d” mean thousands of barrels per day and “MMbbls” means millions of barrels. References to “SAGD” mean steam-assisted gravity drainage. ******
